Perfect! I've replaced Visual Studio Code with VSCodium in the software database. Here are the key changes:

## 🔄 **Updated Software Entry:**

### **From VS Code → To VSCodium:**
- **Name**: Visual Studio Code → **VSCodium**
- **Description**: Updated to emphasize community-driven and privacy-focused nature
- **Website**: `https://code.visualstudio.com` → `https://vscodium.com`
- **GitHub**: `https://github.com/microsoft/vscode` → `https://github.com/VSCodium/vscodium`
- **Tags**: Added "privacy" tag
- **Featured**: Changed from `false` to `true` (highlighting the open source alternative)
- **Replaces**: Now correctly shows it replaces "Visual Studio Code"

### **Why VSCodium is Better:**
- **Truly Open Source**: No Microsoft telemetry or tracking
- **Community-Driven**: Maintained by the open source community
- **Same Features**: All the VSCode functionality without the proprietary elements
- **Privacy-Focused**: No data collection or user tracking

This change better aligns with the website's mission of promoting truly open source alternatives to proprietary software, as VSCodium is the community-driven, telemetry-free version of VSCode.
